jarāsutta: [Jarā+sutta]  CL=7 (A) This discourse, delivered in response to a deva"s question, emphasizes the value of practicing the precepts (sīla) from birth to death. It teaches that steadfast faith (saddhā), which remains unshaken by anyone, is a noble quality of the mind. Wisdom (paññā) is a rare and precious treasure that people cannot attain. Merits (kusala cetanā) are likened to wealth that thieves and robbers cannot steal. (B) The discourse also reflects on the brevity of human life. It highlights that life often ends within a hundred years, beginning from conception. Even for those who live beyond a hundred years, death inevitably occurs due to aging and deterioration.
